Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the intro — excited to get BlueRetail live with Redwood. As part of legal/compliance kickoff, can you share your standard DPA and the current list of subprocessors you require us to disclose? We want to confirm the scope up front so procurement and engineering can align on any architecture changes.

A few items we typically see come up from customers:
- EU->US transfers: are you ok with SCCs or do you require additional safeguards?
- Subprocessor notification vs approval: do you require per-subprocessor approval or is a notification window acceptable?
- Data retention and deletion obligations for backup/snapshots (we retain logs for operational observability by default; customers can request stricter retention).

I'll attach Redwood's standard DPA for your review. If you prefer, we can exchange redlines via DocuSign/AdobeSign and loop in procurement (I assume procurement@blueretail.com is the right contact).

Goal: agree scope and doc execution plan in the next 10 business days so we can finish onboarding.

Thanks —

Vivek,

Thanks for the note. Attaching BlueRetail's standard DPA and our current subprocessor inventory (latest export). A few quick answers:
- We accept SCCs (we use the latest EC standard clauses) but will expect a documented transfer mechanism and a short description of the technical safeguards.
- For subprocessors, we operate on a 10-business-day notification window for non-sensitive subprocessors; anything classified as a "critical" subprocessors requires prior written approval. Please let us know if Redwood classifies any infra providers as critical (e.g., managed KMS or dedicated host).
- Retention: we prefer that operational logs tied to customer identifiers be deleted within 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

Procurement asked that all commercial terms be separated from the DPA redlines; they will only accept an executed DPA once legal rounds are finished. Their contact is procurement@blueretail.com.

We can do a quick 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00am PT if that helps. Otherwise, please send back redlines as a tracked PDF and we will respond.

Regards,
BlueRetail Legal Ops
legalops@blueretail.com

Attachments: BlueRetail_DPA_v1.pdf (stub), BlueRetail_Subprocessors_2026-02.xlsx (stub)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@blueretail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privacy onboarding: subprocessor mapping & DPA exchange — BlueRetail

All — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. Looping in Marissa (legal contact on our side) and Lauren (customer success / onboarding). A few high-level notes from a first pass (we'll send a redline PDF by EOD):

1) SCCs and transfer mechanism: Redwood can accept SCCs and will provide a short transfer description (we use a combination of SCCs + contractual safeguards; for customers who require it, we can also support Binding Corporate Rules if mutually agreed).
2) Subprocessors: our current list includes cloud providers, metrics vendors, and a managed KMS (third-party). We consider our managed KMS to be a critical subprocessor, so we understand that will need prior written approval — we'll flag that in the redline.
3) Retention: we can offer a 90-day default window for operational logs tied to customer identifiers; for customers who require custom retention, we can enable an opt-in policy at contract stage.

Action plan:
- Today: Redwood to return tracked-redline DPA (attached).
- Tomorrow: legal ops to confirm whether the managed KMS counts as a critical subprocessor for BlueRetail and to return a redline of any customer-specific wording.
- If redline exchange is straightforward, execution via DocuSign link (I'll include a placeholder in the redline PDF).

Proposed meeting only if we need to discuss critical-subprocessor boundary. Otherwise the tracked exchange should suffice.

-Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.pdf (tracked-redline stub; contains comments on SCCs, subprocessor approvals, and retention).

Vivek — thanks, Marissa, Lauren.

We reviewed your tracked PDF and have two follow-ups before procurement will accept execution:

1) Please expand the technical description of the transfer mechanism to include whether encryption at-rest keys are customer-controlled or Redwood-managed. That detail will determine whether our security team flags the managed KMS as critical.
2) We would like a clause that provides Redwood's process and timeline for removing customer data from backups and snapshot artifacts (a short, bulletized procedure is fine).

If you can update the tracked PDF with those two clarifications, procurement is OK to progress DocuSign. Otherwise, we're happy to take the 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT to walk through.

Best,
